evidence.claim: MP Materials states in SEC filings that it is the largest producer of rare-earth materials in the Western Hemisphere and has developed rare-earth metal, alloy, and magnet manufacturing in Fort Worth, Texas.
The US Department of Defense awarded MP Materials $35 million to build US heavy rare-earth separation capacity for defense and commercial applications.
evidence.source_title: DoD Awards $35 Million to MP Materials to Build U.S. Heavy Rare Earth Separation Capacity

evidence.claim: Third-party market-cap sources showed MP Materials around $10.5 billion in June 2026, placing it near the upper end of the preferred universe but still relevant as a pure reference anchor.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Market Cap & Net Worth

evidence.claim: Energy Fuels reported production of high-purity NdPr oxide at its White Mesa Mill and described that oxide as part of a mine-to-magnet supply chain independent of China.
Energy Fuels' market cap was reported around $4.3 billion in early June 2026, fitting the preferred USD 300 million to USD 10 billion discovery range.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels Market Cap History Charts

evidence.claim: USA Rare Earth says it is building an integrated rare-earth and permanent magnet supply chain and notes that its Stillwater magnet facility is under development.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth Completes First Commercial Yttrium Metal Production

evidence.claim: USA Rare Earth announced an agreement to acquire Less Common Metals, described as an ex-China rare-earth metal and alloy producer.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth Accelerates Mine-to-Magnet Strategy with the Transformative Acquisition of Less Common Metals

evidence.claim: Third-party market data showed USA Rare Earth around a $5 billion market capitalization in June 2026, placing it in the preferred mid-cap discovery range.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth Stock Price & Overview

evidence.claim: NioCorp says it is developing the Elk Creek Critical Minerals Project in Nebraska and is publicly traded on Nasdaq under ticker NB.
A NioCorp fact sheet describes Elk Creek as a source of niobium, scandium, titanium, and magnetic rare-earth elements important to advanced manufacturing and national security.
Third-party market data placed NioCorp around $700 million to $750 million in June 2026, within the small-cap discovery range.

CNAS noted that the defense industrial base remains shallow and fragile and that DoD often loses visibility beyond tier-two suppliers, supporting the Serenity lens that lower-tier chokepoints can be mispriced.

A non-consensus rare-earth magnet thesis is that the market may count headline ex-China magnet capacity while missing whether oxide, metal, alloy, and magnet lines are qualified on non-Chinese feedstock.
evidence.source_title: The Market Counted Mines. It Missed Magnets. — ForcedAlpha Casefile

memory_update.text: MP should remain the reference benchmark for US rare-earth magnet-chain qualification because it spans mine, separation, metal/alloy, and NdFeB magnet manufacturing, but its size and attention level make it less suitable as the main underfollowed alpha lane.

Energy Fuels is a high-priority underfollowed follow-up because the market may still categorize it as uranium while its rare-earth oxide and heavy-REE separation progress could matter if feedstock provenance becomes the binding constraint.

USA Rare Earth is a direct but execution-sensitive candidate; monitor whether Stillwater and LCM convert nominal capacity into commercial and defense-qualified non-Chinese-feedstock magnet-chain output.
NioCorp belongs in a speculative shadow list, not the core direct list, until evidence improves on financing, construction, separated magnetic-REE output, and magnet-customer qualification.
For this node, the key gating question is not only rare-earth resource ownership but proof of compliant oxide-to-metal-to-alloy-to-magnet qualification for defense or defense-adjacent customers.

Need a later pass on non-US primary listings and ADR/OTC names such as Lynas and Neo Performance, plus private magnet makers such as Vulcan Elements, because US-listed-only screening may miss actual qualified capacity.

node: Rare-earth magnets and non-Chinese feedstock qualification for defense systems
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct US-listed universe around the rare-earth magnet and non-Chinese-feedstock qualification node. The strongest direct reference anchor is MP Materials, which now spans mining, separation, metal/alloy, and magnet manufacturing. The underfollowed lane includes Energy Fuels as a US rare-earth oxide processor with NdPr and heavy-REE oxide relevance, USA Rare Earth as a newly public integrated mine-to-magnet developer with Stillwater magnet capacity and LCM alloy exposure, and NioCorp as a speculative small-cap upstream critical-minerals developer with magnetic rare-earth optionality but weaker current magnet-chain qualification evidence. Key falsification risk: nominal ex-China capacity may not translate into defense-qualified, non-Chinese-feedstock-compliant supply.
